source_refs.note: Topic 6.11.2, printed pages 136-137, with Quick Check 6.8 as the self-check.

blocks.text: Entropies of different substances can be compared by the number of particles, physical properties and state. A small number of particles means low entropy: CaCO3 has a higher standard entropy (92.9 J per K per mol) than CaO (39.7), because the number of possible arrangements is lower when there are fewer particles. Among substances of similar chemical nature, harder substances have lower entropy than softer ones: diamond has lower entropy than graphite because it is much harder, its stronger forces limiting vibration and reducing the probability of disorder. A substance has lower entropy as a solid than as a liquid or a gas: ice near its melting point has 48.0 J per K per mol, water 69.9, and water vapour just above the boiling point 188.7.
